subject: Numeracy
title: Long, longer, longest
objectives: Children will compare two objects by length.
Children will measure with hand spans or steps.
content: Long and short, longer and shorter, and measuring with hands and steps.
teachingActivities: Compare lengths by lining objects up at the same starting point; use ropes, ribbons, pencils and children’s own bodies; introduce non-standard units such as hand spans and cubes; stress that we start at the same line and count the units without gaps.
learnerActivities: Compare two objects by length and measure a short object with hands or cubes.
resources: Ropes and ribbons of different lengths
Pictures of long and short animals
assessment: Observe whether each child says which of two objects is longer and measures with cubes or hands.
expectedOutcomes: Says which of two is longer.
Measures a short object with hands or cubes.

lessons.title: Long and short
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say long and short for different objects.
successCriteria: Finds a long and a short object
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare and order objects by size.
resources: A long rope and a short rope
A long and a short pencil
Pictures of a snake and a worm
lessons.starter: Hold up a long rope and a short rope and say "This is long. This is short."
teacherActivities: Show pairs of objects and say long or short.
Ask "Which is long?" for each pair.
Let children find long and short things in the room.
Stretch long and curl short with bodies.
learnerActivities: Children point to the long one.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pairs of objects and say long or short. Children: Children repeat the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which is long?" for each pair. Children: Children point to the long one.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children find long and short things in the room. Children: Child finds objects.
Step 4. Teacher: Stretch long and curl short with bodies. Children: Children stretch and curl.

practical.title: Long and short hunt
practical.safety: Keep ropes short enough that they are not a strangling risk and supervise closely. Do not let children wrap ropes around necks.

differentiation.support: Offer two very different lengths first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find something as long as their arm.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the snake long or short?
Is the worm long or short?

lessons.conclusion: Stretch long and curl short and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about long and short things you see.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say long and short for different objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Longer and shorter
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will compare two objects and say which is longer or shorter.
successCriteria: Lines up objects at the same start
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare and order objects by size.
lessons.starter: Line up two ribbons at the same place and say "This one is longer. This one is shorter."
teacherActivities: Show how to line up two objects at the same start.
Let children compare pairs of objects.
learnerActivities: Child points to the longer one.
Child points to the shorter one.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to line up two objects at the same start. Children: Children watch and say start.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which is longer?" Children: Child points to the longer one.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which is shorter?" Children: Child points to the shorter one.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children compare pairs of objects. Children: Child compares and says longer.

practical.title: Line up and compare
steps: Put two objects at the same start.
practical.safety: Keep ribbons short and supervise closely. Never let children tie ropes round themselves or friends.

differentiation.support: Compare objects that are very different in length.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find something longer than a pencil.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Lines up objects at the same start
lessons.conclusion: Put the ribbons away and say longer and shorter.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two pencils or spoons at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "compare two objects and say which is longer or shorter" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Longest and shortest
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will order three objects by length.
successCriteria: Puts three objects in order by length
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare and order objects by size.
lessons.starter: Show three ropes and say "Which is the longest? Which is the shortest?"
teacherActivities: Line three ropes at the same start and order them.
Mix them up and ask a child to order them.
Let each child order a set of three.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Line three ropes at the same start and order them. Children: Children watch and say longest.
Step 2. Teacher: Mix them up and ask a child to order them. Children: Child orders the ropes.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which is the shortest?" Children: Child points to the shortest.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child order a set of three. Children: Child orders objects.

practical.title: Order by length
steps: Line them up at the same start.
practical.safety: Use short pieces of soft rope and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Order two objects first and then add a third.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to order five objects.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the sets away and say longest and shortest.
lessons.homeConnection: Order three spoons by length at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "order three objects by length" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Measuring with cubes and hands
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will measure an object with cubes or hand spans and say how many.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare and order objects by size.
resources: Objects to measure such as a book or a table
lessons.starter: Say "How long is our book? Let us measure it with cubes."
teacherActivities: Show how to line cubes along the book with no gaps.
Compare: "Which is longer, the book or the shoe?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to line cubes along the book with no gaps. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Count the cubes together. Children: Children count the cubes.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children measure other objects. Children: Child measures and counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Compare: "Which is longer, the book or the shoe?" Children: Child compares the counts.

practical.title: Measure with cubes
practical.safety: Use cubes too big to swallow and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear of cubes after.

differentiation.support: Measure with hand spans and count together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to measure with two different units.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cubes away and count them.
lessons.homeConnection: Measure a spoon or a shoe with your hand.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "measure an object with cubes or hand spans and say how many" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 length check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child compares and measures lengths.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare and order objects by size.
lessons.starter: Sing the long and short song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: compare, order and measure.
At each station ask "Which is longer?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: compare, order and measure. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Which is longer?" and watch. Children: Child answers and measures.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Length stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use soft short ropes and large cubes. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and compare two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to measure and compare three objects.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says long and short; says longer and shorter; orders three by length; measures with cubes or hands.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
Compares and measures length with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child compares and measures lengths" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
